title: A Cipher for the Autopsy
premise: Retired detective Sable Okafor buried her estranged mentor, Coroner Ada Voss, only to receive a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral — a letter claiming Ada's death was murder and naming a cipher hidden in her autopsy ledgers. As Sable decodes the ledger, she uncovers that Ada falsified cause-of-death rulings decades ago to protect a family from a killer who is still alive, and that the inheritance at stake — a waterfront estate and its dark secrets — has drawn the killer back to finish the job. The final cipher entry points to Ada's own autopsy report, where Sable finds proof of poison and the killer's identity: Ada's devoted protégé, Dr. Elias Marsh, who killed her when she threatened to confess. In a confrontation at the estate, Sable chooses love for Ada's memory over her own safety, exposing Marsh and honoring the duty Ada died trying to fulfill.
about_author: Ulyana Dunmore is a former forensic archivist who spent twelve years cataloguing cold-case files before turning to fiction. She writes mysteries from a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the Baltic coast, where the fog does half her plotting for her.

chapters.title: Postmarked Grief
chapters.summary: Sable Okafor, three weeks into retirement and drowning in a failing bookshop's debts, attends the sparsely attended funeral of Coroner Ada Voss, the woman who trained her. That night an envelope arrives — Ada's handwriting, a confession, postmarked the day after the burial. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: grief curdling into suspicion; the dead do not mail letters.

chapters.title: The Ledger in Plain Sight
chapters.summary: Sable rereads the confession: Ada admits to falsifying autopsy rulings in 1989 and hides 'the truth in the ledger everyone reads.' Searching Ada's donated effects, now shelved in Sable's own shop, she finds a first-edition anatomy text whose marginal numbers form a substitution cipher keyed to case files. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: reluctant reawakening of the detective instinct she swore off.

chapters.title: Nine Rulings, One Lie
chapters.summary: Decoding reveals nine 1989 death certificates altered from homicide to accident or suicide — all victims connected to the Harrow shipping family's estate. Sable visits the county archive and discovers someone else requested the same files last week. POV: Sable, with a brief flashback to young Sable under Ada's tutelage. Emotional beat: dread — she is not the only one reading.

chapters.title: The Heir Apparent
chapters.summary: At the reading of Ada's will, Sable meets the beneficiaries: Dr. Elias Marsh, Ada's grieving protégé; Vivian Harrow, heir to the estate; and a nervous solicitor with ink-stained fingers. The will leaves Sable Ada's 'professional papers' — the ledger itself. POV: Sable observing the room like a crime scene. Emotional beat: every mourner is also a suspect.

chapters.title: What the Water Keeps
chapters.summary: Sable investigates the ninth victim, a dockworker pulled from the harbor in 1989, and finds his daughter, Nia, who has spent thirty years petitioning to reopen the case — and who mailed Ada threatening letters. But Nia's alibi for Ada's death holds. POV: alternating Sable and Nia. Emotional beat: the price of survival paid across generations.

chapters.title: A Second Autopsy
chapters.summary: Marsh blocks Sable's request to exhume Ada, citing protocol with unsettling fluency. Sable notices he quotes the confession's phrasing verbatim — details never made public. When she confronts him gently, he deflects, but that night her bookshop is ransacked and the cipher key stolen. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: fear arriving late, as it always does.

chapters.title: The Tenth Entry
chapters.summary: Sable reconstructs the cipher from memory and decodes a tenth entry added weeks before Ada's death: 'He knows. If I die, look inside me.' She realizes Ada anticipated her own murder and hid evidence in her body — a capsule swallowed before death. POV: Sable, racing the coroner's scheduled cremation. Emotional beat: desperate tenderness; Ada trusted her after all.

chapters.title: Ashes and Arsenic
chapters.summary: Sable halts the cremation hours before it begins; the delayed autopsy recovers a microfilm capsule containing the original 1989 reports and a named accomplice — the solicitor, who confesses that Marsh orchestrated both the old cover-up and Ada's poisoning to protect the estate's inheritance and his own legacy. POV: Sable and the solicitor's interrogation. Emotional beat: vindication shadowed by betrayal.

chapters.title: The Estate at Ebb Tide
chapters.summary: Marsh flees to the Harrow estate to destroy the remaining physical evidence and silence Vivian, the last witness. Sable deduces his destination from tide charts annotated in Ada's ledger and goes alone, knowing police will be too slow. POV: Sable, then Marsh. Emotional beat: love against duty — she goes not for justice alone, but because Ada deserves to be answered.

chapters.title: A Cipher for the Autopsy
chapters.summary: In the estate's boathouse, Marsh confesses with chilling calm — survival required it, he says — before turning on Sable; Vivian intervenes, and Sable subdues him as sirens arrive. Weeks later, Sable reopens the bookshop, shelves Ada's anatomy text in the window, and finally grieves. POV: Sable. Emotional beat: resolution — some inheritances are duties, and she accepts hers.
